block_classes.note: perception only: an unexposed cell in the voxel window (DESIGN.md 6.1); never in a world

exceptions.approximation: the simulator crafts a bed from any three wool; in the real game the three wool must share a colour (sim-to-real check in M7)
exceptions.justification: each bed recipe needs three wool of one colour (and dyeing recipes need dyes, not v1)

exceptions.approximation: these recipes are left out of the class-level recipe book (they only lose material)
exceptions.justification: wood and stripped-wood recipes turn four logs of one wood type into three logs of the same class

exceptions.approximation: the class drops once per object (as the half named in drop_state); the simulator must break both cells together, so a loot condition that tests the other half (tall grass, large fern) is taken as true
exceptions.justification: two-cell object: one half drops nothing and breaking either half removes both

exceptions.approximation: they keep the wall's 1.5 collision class
exceptions.justification: wall states with no post and no sides have no collision box but cannot occur in normal play

exceptions.approximation: blocks destroyed by explosions drop as if broken by a player
exceptions.justification: drops are specialised to a player breaking the block without enchantments (DESIGN.md 4.2: no Fortune or Silk Touch) and without an explosion

exceptions.approximation: water inside slabs, stairs, fences and similar blocks is ignored
exceptions.justification: waterlogged states keep the class of the dry state

exceptions.approximation: block light from state-dependent sources is taken as the block's data value
exceptions.justification: light emission is per block in the data (lit furnaces, lit redstone ore and redstone lamps are not distinguished)
